text:
elena: Heads up — AcmeCorp-SRE reporting 403 on POST /v1/generate using a service key. Embeddings endpoint works. Pasted curl and error below. Can someone triage? :eyes:

AcmeCorp-SRE: curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer svc_ABC' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-large\",\"input\":\"hello\"}'

AcmeCorp-SRE: Response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{ \"error\": \"insufficient_scope\", \"message\": \"key lacks generation permissions\" }

sam: Thanks — can you paste the decoded JWT payload (redact any IDs), and which embeddings endpoint you called that succeeded?

AcmeCorp-SRE: embeddings call was POST /v1/embeddings with same key — returned 200. Decoded payload (redacted):
```
{ \"sub\": \"svc_987\", \"entitlements\": [\"embeddings\", \"converse\", \"rerank\"], \"iss\": \"sso.acmecorp\", \"exp\": 1765000000 }
```

sam: Looks like the token includes \"converse\" but not the canonical \"inference\" or \"generate\" entitlement. Our auth normalizer only recognizes certain aliases. If \"converse\" isn't mapped to \"inference\" it will be dropped during claim canonicalization and the token ends up without generation permission.

niko: Confirmed. Alias table mappings currently: \"gen\" -> \"inference\", \"embed\" / \"vect\" -> \"embeddings\", \"rerank\" -> \"rerank\". No mapping for \"converse\". Unknown aliases are excluded (not forwarded) by the normalizer.

elena: Account team said IdP template was changed last week and they started using an app scope named \"converse\". That would explain why freshly provisioned svc keys are failing for generation.

sam: Repro I ran locally: 1) minted JWT with entitlements=[\"converse\",\"embeddings\"]; 2) POST /v1/generate -> 403 insufficient_scope; 3) POST /v1/embeddings -> 200.

Auth log snippet:
```
WARN auth-normalizer: unknown-entitlement=\"converse\" sub=svc_987 -> dropped
```

niko: Root cause: provisioning/sync flow writes IdP-provided scope \"converse\" into the token. Normalizer doesn't map it to \"inference\", so downstream auth checks fail for generation requests.

elena: Short-term mitigation: create/rotate a service key that explicitly includes the \"inference\" entitlement (Console or CLI). That will unblock their generation calls immediately.

AcmeCorp-SRE: Can you share the CLI snippet? We automate key rotation via scripts.

elena: Example using redwoodctl (redacted org flags):
```
redwoodctl keys create --tenant acmecorp --scopes inference,embeddings --output json
```

niko: Long-term fix: I'll open a PR to add alias mapping \"converse\" -> \"inference\" and \"converse.v1\" variants, plus add a telemetry alert for any dropped-entitlement events > 0 during tenant syncs. PR: https://git.redwood/infer/auth-normalizer/pull/511 (WIP). Will include unit tests and a canary rollout plan.

inc-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1407 — entitlement-aliasing causing 403 on /v1/generate for some SSO-provisioned keys. Tags: eng-auth, customer-success, support-p1.

acct-team: Looping in AcmeCorp AMs and security to coordinate rotation and confirm compliance.

AcmeCorp-SRE: Rotated new key with explicit \"inference\" scope via redwoodctl. Re-tested: POST /v1/generate -> 200 OK. Thanks.

elena: Excellent. We'll keep incident open until mapping PR is merged, deployed, and we run a tenant resync for affected customers. Closing plan: 1) short-term rotation (done), 2) merge alias mapping + tests, 3) update SCIM template for known IdPs, 4) run targeted sync, 5) close incident.

sam: I'll add a short KB note for Support describing the \"converse\" alias and the temporary CLI workaround.

elena: Thanks everyone — leaving the incident open until we see the deploy + resync complete. :white_check_mark:
